summary.text: Scholten is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 3rd District, first elected in 2022. A fourth-generation West Michigander, she worked as a social worker and then as an immigration attorney, including at the U.S. Department of Justice's Board of Immigration Appeals and the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center. She is seeking a third term.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1982 in Michigan and raised in the Hudsonville area; her official biography describes her as a fourth-generation West Michigander whose mother was a public school teacher. According to Wikipedia, her father was a sports journalist at The Grand Rapids Press.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Gordon College and a law degree from the University of Maryland School of Law. Sources differ on the graduation years, so they are omitted.

Began her career as a social worker, working with people affected by housing and homelessness issues, according to her official biography; her campaign site says she was a case worker for the AIDS Action Committee.

After law school clerked for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit in its unit focused on immigration, then joined the U.S. Department of Justice through the Attorney General's Honors Program, working on immigration and civil rights matters.

Served as an attorney adviser with the Justice Department's Board of Immigration Appeals (2013-2017, per Wikipedia), then as a staff attorney at the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center and as senior counsel at Miller Johnson; her campaign site also lists volunteer work as an attorney for the Time's Up Legal Defense Fund.
Ran for the 3rd District in 2020 and lost to Republican Peter Meijer, 47% to 53%.

Won the seat in 2022, defeating Republican John Gibbs 55% to 42%, and took office in January 2023; her official biography says she is the first woman and mother to represent the district. Wikipedia reports she was re-elected in 2024 with 53.7% of the vote.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026: Small Business and Transportation and Infrastructure.
According to her official biography she lives on the southeast side of Grand Rapids, where she is raising two sons.
Was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.
